questions.question: The heading reads "AT 28 February" because the statement presents:
options: A position at a moment — balances existing as the clock strikes, not flows over a period

questions.question: The statement's skeleton is:
options: The accounting equation presented formally — assets on one side, equity and liabilities on the other, totals agreeing
The trial balance in two columns

questions.question: Current is separated from non-current by:
options: A TIME test — one year — applied to both sides of the statement

questions.question: The statement balances because:
options: The bookkeeper forces the final totals
Assets are always adjusted to match
Every double entry, adjustment and closing kept the equation level — the page exhibits that inheritance

questions.question: Fixed assets appear on the statement at:
options: CARRYING VALUE — cost R18 000 less accumulated depreciation R1 800 = R16 200, with the detail in the note

questions.question: Inventories of R2 450 combine:
options: Trading stock R2 250 plus consumable stores on hand R200

questions.question: Trade and other receivables of R4 950 assemble:
options: Creditors, accrued expenses and income in advance
Trade debtors R3 850 plus accrued income R500 plus prepaid expenses R600

questions.question: The current asset families conventionally run:
options: From least to most liquid — inventories, then receivables, then cash and cash equivalents

questions.question: Closing owner's equity of R23 900 is built as:
options: Opening capital R20 000 plus net profit R7 900 less drawings R4 000
Opening capital plus drawings less profit
The bank balance plus the profit

questions.question: The single most examined link between the two statements is:
options: The income statement's net profit arriving as a LINE ITEM in the equity movement
The bank balance matching the cash journal
Depreciation appearing twice on one page

questions.question: The loan appears among non-current liabilities at:
options: Its CAPITALISED balance of R11 200 — grown by the unpaid interest

questions.question: Trade and other payables of R3 800 assemble:
options: Trade creditors R3 200 plus accrued expenses R100 plus income received in advance R500

subtopics.title: Where the Adjustments Landed, and Technique

questions.question: Depreciation appears in the statements:
options: TWICE — the year's charge on the income statement, the accumulated total reducing fixed assets here
Once, on the income statement only
Nowhere — it is a note item only

questions.question: Prepaid expenses and accrued income both file under:
options: Trade and other receivables — benefit arriving within the year

questions.question: The note reference column exists so that:
options: A marker can travel from any statement line to its note and find the same figure at both ends

questions.question: If the two totals disagree, the usual suspects are:
options: A missing adjustment twin, drawings left out of equity, or the loan at its uncapitalised figure

questions.question: The movie and the photograph differ in that:
options: The movie tells the year's story of flows; the photograph freezes what the shop holds at one midnight
They are two copies of the same page

questions.question: The photograph's two walls are:
options: What the shop HOLDS, and who PROVIDED it

questions.question: The two walls must weigh the same because:
options: Nothing in the shop appeared from nowhere — everything owned was funded by somebody

subtopics.title: Two Piles That Must Weigh the Same

questions.question: The one question that sorts the whole photograph is:
options: How soon does this turn into money, or demand money?
Is it a debit or a credit?

questions.question: The fast pile's three pockets are:
options: Inventories; money on its way in (receivables); money already here (cash)

questions.question: Fast assets R22 700 against fast debts R3 800 lets a reader see at a glance:
options: What's coming due can be covered nearly six times by what's coming in — the seed of liquidity analysis

questions.question: "The sorting isn't decoration" because:
options: The layout itself performs the first analysis — speed-sorted piles reveal the next twelve months

subtopics.title: The Owner's Jar, Opened and Closed

questions.question: The jar's three moves to R23 900 are:
options: Opened at R20 000, plus profit R7 900 poured in, minus drawings R4 000 dipped out
Opened at R20 000, plus drawings, minus profit
Opened at zero, plus capital, plus loan

questions.question: "The connected pipes" between the statements means:
options: The movie's final line — net profit — pours into the photograph's jar as part of equity
Cash flows from one page to the other
The notes join the pages physically

questions.question: Drawings never touch the profit story because:
options: They are too small to record
The owner simply took his own money out early — it comes straight from the jar, not from the earning
They were paid in goods, not cash

questions.question: The page's final act — both walls at R38 900 — exhibits:
options: The equation, unbroken through three terms of transactions, adjustments and closings
